wa_darrington.blurb: Darrington sits in the North Cascades foothills east of the I-5 corridor, reached by Highway 530, and its climbing is spread over domes and buttresses in the Clear Creek and Squire Creek drainages south of town. Trad is the main event, with long multi-pitch routes, plus a good supply of sport climbs and a sizable bouldering contingent, much of it shaded, in the White Chuck River drainage. Roped grades cluster from 5.8 to 5.10 with some 5.11, and boulder problems run from V0 to V7. Three O'clock Rock offers big clean slabby buttresses facing northeast, and Exfoliation Dome and Spring Mountain add more. Rainfall is heavy, so allow time for rock to dry.

ca_monkeyface_falls.blurb: Monkeyface Falls is a shady slot canyon in the San Bernardino Mountains, reached from Highway 38 across a talus field in about fifteen minutes. Waterfalls run through it and trees keep it cool, which makes it a favored summer sport destination, though it climbs well year-round. Sport routes make up the larger share, mostly 5.9 to 5.12 with a handful harder, spread along both sides of the canyon. The Secret Passage lies deeper in and involves some class 4 scrambling, and solid rappelling skills are useful. The Monkeyface Boulders add about eighty problems, many of them easy, so there is something for newer climbers too.

ut_wasatch_back.blurb: The Wasatch Back is the eastern side of the Wasatch Range around Park City, better known for skiing than climbing, with sport climbing as its main draw. Echo Canyon is the center of it: bolted cobble conglomerate on walls that face southwest through southeast, with pockets, slopers, crimps and jugs, and most of the best lines gathered at the Dry Wall. Grades run from about 5.9 to 5.13, thickest at 5.12 and 5.13. Around Park City, scattered boulders such as Empire Pass and Guardsman add easy to moderate bouldering, and the Echo to Henefer corridor holds winter ice from WI2 to WI5.

ky_cathedral_domain_climbing_area_cdca.blurb: Cathedral Domain is a newer and still growing climbing area in the Red River Gorge region of eastern Kentucky, known as a quieter alternative to the busier cliffs elsewhere in the gorge. It is almost entirely sport climbing, with a few trad lines, spread over some thirty small crags and walls. Grades run from 5.4 to 5.12 but concentrate heavily at 5.10 and 5.11, with a decent number of 5.8 and 5.9 lines for newer leaders. Among the larger sectors are White Pine Trail, Pumpkin Patch, East Coast Crag, Blue Sky and Knowhere Wall. With so many compact crags, expect to move around a lot in a day.
